calls.summary: Daniel Wathne (GrowthBook sales) and Logan Bates (solutions engineering) demonstrated the GrowthBook experimentation and feature flagging platform to Picnic’s team (Jip, Brian, Xavi, Stefan). They addressed Picnic’s pain points: fragmented manual workflows, lack of an experimentation framework, no historical record of tests, and inability to monitor experiments in real time. Next steps: Picnic will debrief internally and follow up with Daniel to decide on a trial or further questions; Daniel

calls.title: Growthbook <> Picnic - POC Scoping/Kickoff
calls.summary: The meeting outlined a three-week proof of concept (POC) for integrating GrowthBook into Picnic's operations, beginning with integration tasks in the first week, followed by conducting an experiment in the second week and reviewing results in the final week. The goals include validating the connection between GrowthBook and Picnic's data infrastructure, enhancing the ease of running experiments, and considering feature flag evaluations later. Resource allocation will involve 1-2 weeks of effort from developers and analysts with minimal disruption to ongoing projects. The importance of security reviews was highlighted, with a checklist provided by GrowthBook to clarify requirements. Additionally, the POC will be free of charge, with deployment options discussed, favoring a cloud-managed setup.
calls.keywords: Growthbook, Proof of Concept, Snowflake Integration, Experimentation, Feature Flags, Security Review

calls.title: Growthbook <> Picnic - Experimentation Best Practice Session
calls.summary: Participants discussed the importance of aligning experimentation goals with strategic metrics to enhance the quality of insights derived from experiments. Misaligned experiments currently lead to inconclusive results, wasting resources and causing decision fatigue. Stefan highlighted the need for standardized customer journey metrics to better understand customer behavior across stages. Luke emphasized the significance of coordinated team metrics to prevent cannibalization and facilitate faster learning. The discussion also covered offline and online experimentation, advocating for offline validation as a quality gate. GrowthBook's capabilities were reviewed, noting its support for metric standardization and the limitations in guiding decisions beyond basic outcomes. Overall, the conversation aimed to enhance organizational alignment and cultivate a culture that maximizes the value of experimentation.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Metrics, Offline Evaluation, Online Testing, GrowthBook, Customer Journeys
